# Guarded cell -- OpenPLC starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The program's logic section is yours.*

**The task.** Run the transfer cell without ever writing belt.rotate. You command starter.coil; the contactor runs the motor. The safety relay watches one interlock contact from each leaf of the cell gate and holds your coil off until both leaves are shut and somebody presses Reset — so the relay closing hands the coil back and starts nothing. Cartons have to cross the scanner's protective field, so bridge it with scanner.mute while each one passes; the panel's pot is how long you bridge it for. Then transfer each carton into the chute with the cylinder, sequencing on the two reeds and never energising both coils.

**Done when.** Cartons reach transferred.count while your program has never written belt.rotate — belt.rotate follows starter.aux, because the contactor runs the motor and you only run the coil. Opening either gate leaf stops the cell inside 200 ms; closing both and pressing Reset lights relay.k1 and starts nothing at all, and Start is what starts it. Open one leaf on its own and, past the relay's sync window, relay.fault latches: a reset while it is still open will not clear it. Finally turn the pot past the scanner's own mute limit and watch scanner.muted go out while scanner.mute is still commanded — your mute stopped being a mute, the next carton in the field stopped the cell, and that is what a mute without a limit hides.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`guarded_cell.st`](guarded_cell.st) | Every I/O point declared at its located address, with an empty logic section. |
| [`mbconfig.cfg`](mbconfig.cfg) | The Slave Device entry that points OpenPLC's Modbus master at the sidecar. |

The walkthrough for OpenPLC itself -- installing, compiling, timing,
troubleshooting -- is [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md). This page
is only what is different about this scene.

## Run it

1. Open the scene in FactoryForge: pick "Guarded cell" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/guarded_cell.json).
2. **Then** start the sidecar as the Modbus slave. The order matters: the
   addresses below are the ones it hands out for this scene's tags, and a
   sidecar that was already running when you changed scene keeps its old
   addresses and puts the new tags above them.

   ```bash
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp -o port 5502
   ```

   (From a source checkout: `cd sidecar && python -m factoryforge_sidecar connect ...`.
   If OpenPLC runs in WSL or a VM, add `-o host 0.0.0.0` and read the warning
   it prints.) Check the address map it prints against the table below.
3. Compile `guarded_cell.st` in OpenPLC (web UI *Programs -> Upload*, or copy it
   into `webserver/st_files/` and run `./scripts/compile_program.sh guarded_cell.st`)
   and copy `mbconfig.cfg` to `webserver/core/`,
   or enter these numbers in *Slave Devices -> Add new device*
   (Generic Modbus TCP device, port 5502, slave id 1):

| Block | Start | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Discrete Inputs (%IX100.0) | 0 | 24 |
| Coils (%QX100.0) | 1 | 13 |
| Input Registers (%IW100) | 0 | 8 |
| Holding Registers - Read (%IW100) | 0 | 0 |
| Holding Registers - Write (%QW100) | 0 | 0 |

4. Start the PLC. To have it marked instead, run the grader in place of the
   3D scene -- same tags, same addresses -- and pass the port it prints:

   ```bash
   python tools/grade.py --scene guarded-cell
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp --port <bus port it printed> -o port 5502
   ```

## I/O

`PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp); `PLC reads` is an input
(a sensor, a button, a measurement). *Brief* marks the signals the task names;
the rest are there to be used, such as each drive's fault contact. Modbus
addresses are decimal, as the sidecar prints them: `0x10` is coil ten.

| Tag | Direction | Type | Modbus | In the program | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `belt.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x0 | `BeltFault` %IX100.0 | drive fault: TRUE = faulted; a faulted drive does not turn, whatever it is told |  |
| `belt.rotate` | PLC writes | bit | not wired | -- | starter.coil's contactor drives it; a program that writes it fails this exercise |  |
| `cylinder.extend` | PLC writes | bit | 0x1 | `CylinderExtend` %QX100.0 | extend coil (5/2 valve, no spring: the rod stays where it was last driven) | yes |
| `cylinder.extended` | PLC reads | bit | 1x1 | `CylinderExtended` %IX100.1 | reed switch at full stroke | yes |
| `cylinder.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x2 | `CylinderFault` %IX100.2 | TRUE = the cylinder has seized |  |
| `cylinder.retract` | PLC writes | bit | 0x2 | `CylinderRetract` %QX100.1 | retract coil | yes |
| `cylinder.retracted` | PLC reads | bit | 1x3 | `CylinderRetracted` %IX100.3 | reed switch at home; mid-stroke neither reed is made | yes |
| `emitter.emit` | PLC writes | bit | 0x3 | `EmitterEmit` %QX100.2 | rising edge = feed one carton; hold each level well over one poll | yes |
| `guard_a.closed` | PLC reads | bit | 1x4 | `GuardAClosed` %IX100.4 | guard switch, normally closed: TRUE while the door is shut | yes |
| `guard_a.lock` | PLC writes | bit | 0x4 | `GuardALock` %QX100.3 | energise the solenoid lock (it only bites on a shut door) |  |
| `guard_a.locked` | PLC reads | bit | 1x5 | `GuardALocked` %IX100.5 | TRUE while the door is locked shut |  |
| `guard_b.closed` | PLC reads | bit | 1x6 | `GuardBClosed` %IX100.6 | guard switch, normally closed: TRUE while the door is shut | yes |
| `guard_b.lock` | PLC writes | bit | 0x5 | `GuardBLock` %QX100.4 | energise the solenoid lock (it only bites on a shut door) |  |
| `guard_b.locked` | PLC reads | bit | 1x7 | `GuardBLocked` %IX100.7 | TRUE while the door is locked shut |  |
| `line_end.count` | PLC reads | int | 3x0 + 3x1 | `LineEndCountHi` %IW100 + `LineEndCountLo` %IW101 -> `LineEndCount` : DINT | cartons this remover has taken off the line, running total |  |
| `mute_eye.detect` | PLC reads | bit | 1x8 | `MuteEyeDetect` %IX101.0 | TRUE while a carton is in the beam | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x9 | `PanelEstop` %IX101.1 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x6 | `PanelGreen` %QX100.5 | green lamp on the panel | yes |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x7 | `PanelRed` %QX100.6 | red lamp on the panel | yes |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | bit | 1x10 | `PanelReset` %IX101.2 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | float | 3x2 + 3x3 | `PanelSetpointHi` %IW102 + `PanelSetpointLo` %IW103 -> `PanelSetpoint` : REAL | the operator's pot, 1..10 s (starts at 3.5) | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | bit | 1x11 | `PanelStart` %IX101.3 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x12 | `PanelStop` %IX101.4 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `push_eye.detect` | PLC reads | bit | 1x13 | `PushEyeDetect` %IX101.5 | TRUE while a carton is in the beam | yes |
| `relay.cha` | PLC reads | bit | 1x14 | `RelayCha` %IX101.6 | channel A as the relay sees it (guard_a.closed) |  |
| `relay.chb` | PLC reads | bit | 1x15 | `RelayChb` %IX101.7 | channel B as the relay sees it (guard_b.closed) |  |
| `relay.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x16 | `RelayFault` %IX102.0 | TRUE = the two channels disagreed; the relay latches this fault | yes |
| `relay.k1` | PLC reads | bit | 1x17 | `RelayK1` %IX102.1 | safety contact K1: TRUE while the relay's outputs are closed (open, they hold starter.coil FALSE) | yes |
| `relay.k2` | PLC reads | bit | 1x18 | `RelayK2` %IX102.2 | safety contact K2: TRUE while the relay's outputs are closed | yes |
| `relay.reset` | PLC writes | bit | 0x8 | `RelayReset` %QX100.7 | reset: the relay closes on a RISING edge, and only with both channels healthy | yes |
| `scanner.mute` | PLC writes | bit | 0x9 | `ScannerMute` %QX101.0 | request muting; honoured for at most 6 s at a stretch | yes |
| `scanner.muted` | PLC reads | bit | 1x19 | `ScannerMuted` %IX102.3 | TRUE while muting is actually in force | yes |
| `scanner.stop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x20 | `ScannerStop` %IX102.4 | protective field clear, normally closed: TRUE = clear, FALSE = someone is in it | yes |
| `scanner.warn` | PLC reads | bit | 1x21 | `ScannerWarn` %IX102.5 | TRUE while the warning field is broken | yes |
| `starter.aux` | PLC reads | bit | 1x22 | `StarterAux` %IX102.6 | auxiliary contact: TRUE while the contactor has really pulled in | yes |
| `starter.coil` | PLC writes | bit | 0x10 | `StarterCoil` %QX101.1 | contactor coil -- the contactor runs belt.rotate | yes |
| `starter.current` | PLC reads | float | 3x4 + 3x5 | `StarterCurrentHi` %IW104 + `StarterCurrentLo` %IW105 -> `StarterCurrent` : REAL | motor current, A | yes |
| `starter.overload` | PLC reads | bit | 1x23 | `StarterOverload` %IX102.7 | thermal overload, normally closed: TRUE = OK, FALSE = tripped | yes |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x11 | `TowerGreen` %QX101.2 | tower lamp, green |  |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x12 | `TowerRed` %QX101.3 | tower lamp, red |  |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | bit | 0x13 | `TowerYellow` %QX101.4 | tower lamp, yellow |  |
| `transferred.count` | PLC reads | int | 3x6 + 3x7 | `TransferredCountHi` %IW106 + `TransferredCountLo` %IW107 -> `TransferredCount` : DINT | cartons this remover has taken off the line, running total | yes |

## Three things this scene's wiring does not forgive

- **A 32-bit value is two registers**, high word first. This scene has 4:
  `line_end.count`, `panel.setpoint`, `starter.current`, `transferred.count`.
  The program's first and last sections move them between the registers and
  plain DINT/REAL variables, so your logic never sees a register. OpenPLC's
  `DWORD_TO_REAL` converts the *number* (`16#3F800000` becomes 1065353216.0,
  not 1.0), so the starter rebuilds a REAL bit by bit instead.
  [`../check_starters.sh`](../check_starters.sh) compiles the helpers with
  OpenPLC's own matiec and checks them against two million bit patterns.
- **Anything polled can be missed if it is short.** OpenPLC's master reads
  every 50 ms. A button press in the 3D scene is one physics tick (about 17 ms)
  on the tag bus, so a click can fall between two polls; the grader holds each
  press for 0.15 s. The same goes the other way: hold an output you want the
  scene to see for well over one polling period.
- **An output you never write is FALSE.** The master rewrites the whole coil
  block on every poll, including coils your program does not touch.

## Not wired

`belt.rotate`: starter.coil's contactor drives it; a program that writes it fails this exercise. The coil block starts above it, so OpenPLC never writes it.
